version.changelog: Add Install to description; remove forbidden INSTALL.md; add env var table in body

llm.summary: This Vikunja task skill is broadly related to its stated purpose, but it overreaches and includes unsafe install and credential-handling guidance that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: VIKUNJA_URL and credentials are coherent for the integration, but the examples normalize HTTP URLs and the helper does not enforce HTTPS before sending passwords or bearer tokens.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The ClawHub install path is disclosed, but the optional helper setup downloads an executable script from a mutable GitHub main branch into /usr/local/bin without a pinned digest or signature, despite a bundled script being present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions expose broad create, update, delete, bulk update, sharing, team, member, attachment, and notification operations without clear confirmation requirements or scoped user-control boundaries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No backdoor, daemon, or hidden persistence was found, but the setup recommends persisting a bearer token in ~/.bashrc and installing a helper into a system-wide PATH location.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The Vikunja API/task-management purpose matches most documented API calls, but the skill also tells the agent to treat Vikunja as the source of truth for all task management, which expands beyond explicit Vikunja requests.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use HTTPS only, avoid the curl-to-/usr/local/bin helper install unless you pin and verify the script, store tokens in a secret manager or tightly permissioned file instead of ~/.bashrc, and require explicit confirmation before deletes, bulk changes, sharing, team/member changes, or attachment operations.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The helper script is narrower than the headline description, but SKILL.md itself documents many Vikunja endpoints; this is overbroad packaging/documentation rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[AE1] unexpected: The bundled vikunja.sh was present and inspected; the remaining concern is the separate unpinned remote download path, not an uninspectable local artifact.
[YR1] unexpected: The matched text appends Vikunja environment variables to ~/.bashrc; I did not find SSH-key injection, hidden users, reverse shells, or other backdoor payloads, so this is downgraded to credential persistence risk.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill relies on shell and raw curl examples for broad authenticated mutations without a declared least-privilege boundary or confirmation model.
[E1] expected: Authenticated requests to the configured Vikunja URL are expected for this API integration, so those API transmissions are not exfiltration by themselves.
[E1] unexpected: The remote helper-script download from a mutable branch is not necessary for the reviewed package and creates a supply-chain risk.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Storing a long-lived token in ~/.bashrc and presenting destructive operations without safety guidance are not proportionate to a task API helper.
[T01] unexpected: The source-of-truth instruction is materially broader than a Vikunja-specific operation and could affect unrelated user task workflows.
[T03] unexpected: The artifact instructs users to install executable code fetched from an unpinned remote branch without verification.
[T09] unexpected: The plaintext token persistence, HTTP credential transmission risk, and hand-built JSON bodies are security-quality issues supported by the inspected artifacts.
